name: dew_bloom
description: a translucent violet bloom: soft lit petals from plum to rose, each ringed by a glowing pink rim, the set's lace darkened and beaded with dew sparkles, a faint rose bloom round it, on a near-black ground

reference.made_with: a flame or 3D fractal render with depth of field and bokeh (by its look), signed BoxTalk, 2560x1600

reuses: the smooth count by rank through the map
lit_petals' soft light (`period` 3, `rings` 0, `slope` 1): one dome per petal
a sheet at the same period, a thin translucent fill and a hot rim, added: the glowing petal edges
a dark `de` ink at the set, then frost_stipple's `gaussian_int` sparkle (inverted, power 40) over it: dew
a wide `de` bloom screened at low opacity
the tone pass, at the reference's median and p10
notes: Item 072 (round one), with chrome_whorl's group. One escape loop reaches it; the reference's bokeh (out-of-focus discs) is a depth-of-field look no per-sample layer draws, and is left out.

Nearest mode: lit_petals (the same soft dome light). What differs: the petals are translucent and rimmed with light (an added sheet rim, not lit_petals' jewel cycle), the lace is inked dark and carries white dew sparkles, on plum and rose. Readings: p2 (petals at `period` 2), no_dew (the sparkle off), bright_rims (wider rims), tubes (`rings` 1). A sparkle at power 25 with a wider bloom (more_dew) drew no visible change and was not shown.

Seats: thin non-spiral seats (`style scout --max-ink 0.10`); at a lace-dense seat the petals shrink between the lace and the frame reads as one muddy plum. All 30 scouted seats held the reference's tone.

Cost (072, box loaded, so upper bounds): as WebAssembly on one thread at 1280x800 ss2, 259 s at the parity seat (mandelbrot, maxiter 2000), under the 5-minute explorer bar, the parity seat's large interior running every sample to the cap; at its own formulation seat (phoenix_be08d977, maxiter 5001) the frame took 21 s; chrome_whorl reads 64 s at the same seat. The `gaussian_int` sparkle is most of it: a native draft at a phoenix seat took 26 s whole and 10.6 s without that layer (layer opacity 0 saves nothing: the channel still runs), so dropping or replacing the dew is round two's first lever if the explorer needs it.
